title: Are microplastics harming us?
transcript:
Hi Becca.
Hi Phil.
Becca, I've got a question for you. What's the last plastic thing you had in your hands?
Well, I just did my makeup, so probably a makeup brush.
Many of us own lots of things made of plastic. It's cheap, easy to shape and long lasting, but that's not always a good thing. In this episode of 6 Minute English, we'll be hearing from experts as they teach us about microplastics – those are tiny plastic pieces. And we'll be asking the question, 'Are microplastics affecting our health?'
OK. Well, let's start with our quiz, Becca. There was a social media post that says that every week we ingest the same amount of plastic as there is in a credit card, but that's not true.
Oh, thank goodness!
So, my question for you is how long would it really take to ingest that amount of microplastics? Would it be: a) 13,000 years, b) 23,000 years, or c) 33,000 years?
Well, I want to be hopeful, so I'll go with the longest period of time. That would be 33,000 years.
OK. Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
So, the World Health Organisation says that microplastics have been found in many different food groups. But Phil, what is the food group that is more affected by microplastics?
Well, scientists have found that seafood is one of the main food groups where microplastics can be found, and BBC World Service programme The Evidence has been investigating this. Professor Shilpa Chokshi told host Claudia Hammond about some pictures that she was shown by a microplastics expert.
And he showed me all these marine animals that looked like they had plastics in their livers and hind guts. And from that initial discussion, I went away and I looked at the literature and I looked at the data, and there was emerging evidence that there was plastics in the liver, and there was this correlation increase.
Shilpa says that plastics have been found in marine animals. Marine describes anything related to, found in or produced by the sea.
Yes, these pictures of marine animals with plastics in their bodies inspired Shilpa to dive deeper into the data. She found emerging evidence, and the adjective emerging describes something coming into view after being hidden, allowing it to develop or be better understood.
And from this emerging evidence, Shilpa noticed a correlation. You'll hear this word a lot when talking about data. A correlation is a link or connection between two or more things. So, Phil, we know how toxic microplastics get into our body, but are they definitely harmful?
Well, plastics have been a big part of daily life since the 1950s, but it's only recently that we've started thinking about microplastics as a health issue. For example, scientists have been looking at people who worked in nylon factories where they were exposed to high levels of microplastic. And the scientists think that there may be a correlation between this and diseases that they developed later on. Science professor Mark Miodownik, from University College London, has mixed feelings about microplastics and explained these to BBC World Service programme The Evidence.
Well, you know, we have been exposed for decades and surely if it was that bad, you know, we'd have seen a spike or something by now. But on the other hand, you know, I think, you know, if you look at how much plastic packaging is in supermarkets, it's gone up and up and up and up. And this is not a quantified measure, but our exposure seems to be increasing, and that's the worry for me.
Mark mentions that some people say if microplastics were harmful, we surely would have seen a spike in issues related to them by now. A spike is literally a pointy shape, but here it means a sudden, sharp increase in something.
Right. And though the amount of plastic packaging we use has increased, this isn't a quantified measure. If something is quantified, then it's measured and given a number or a value.
So, Mark concludes that he is worried about our exposure to plastics. Exposure means coming into contact with something that may have an impact on you. OK. Phil, so, if people are worried about their exposure to microplastics, what can they do to reduce this?
Well, one thing they can do is to replace things like plastic chopping boards, utensils and food storage containers. And another tip from BBC World Service's The Evidence is to replace tea bags, which often contain microplastics, with loose-leaf tea. OK. Becca, now it's time to get the answer to our quiz question. And I asked you how long it would take to ingest a credit-card-sized amount of microplastics.
Yes, and I said 33,000 years.
OK. Well, I've got two bits of bad news for you, Becca. One, you were wrong. And two, I'm afraid it's only 23,000 years that it would take to ingest that plastic. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with marine, which describes anything related to, found in or produced by the sea.
The adjective emerging describes something coming into view after being hidden, allowing it to develop or be better understood.
A correlation is a relationship between two or more things.
A spike is a sudden, sharp increase in something.
If something is quantified, it's measured and given a number or a value.
And exposure means to come into contact with something that may have an impact on you.
Once again, our six minutes are up. Test what you've learned with the worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

title_translation: 微塑料正在伤害我们吗？

sentences.text: Hi Becca.
sentences.translation: 嗨，贝卡。

sentences.text: Hi Phil.
sentences.translation: 嗨，菲尔。

sentences.text: Becca, I've got a question for you.
sentences.translation: 贝卡，我想问你个问题。

sentences.text: What's the last plastic thing you had in your hands?
sentences.translation: 你上次手里拿的塑料东西是什么？

sentences.text: Well, I just did my makeup,
sentences.translation: 嗯，我刚刚化了妆，

sentences.text: so probably a makeup brush.
sentences.translation: 所以可能是化妆刷吧。

sentences.text: Many of us own lots of things made of plastic.
sentences.translation: 我们很多人都拥有很多塑料制品。

sentences.text: It's cheap, easy to shape and long lasting,
sentences.translation: 它便宜、易塑形又耐用，

sentences.text: but that's not always a good thing.
sentences.translation: 但这并不总是好事。

sentences.text: In this episode of 6 Minute English,
sentences.translation: 在本期《六分钟英语》中，

sentences.text: we'll be hearing from experts as they teach us about microplastics – those are tiny plastic pieces.
sentences.translation: 我们会听到专家讲解微塑料——就是微小的塑料颗粒。

sentences.text: And we'll be asking the question,
sentences.translation: 我们还会探讨这个问题：

sentences.text: 'Are microplastics affecting our health?'
sentences.translation: “微塑料会影响我们的健康吗？”

sentences.text: OK.
sentences.translation: 好的。

sentences.text: Well, let's start with our quiz, Becca.
sentences.translation: 那我们先从问答开始吧，贝卡。

sentences.text: There was a social media post that says that every week we ingest the same amount of plastic as there is in a credit card,
sentences.translation: 有一条社交媒体帖子说，我们每周摄入的塑料量相当于一张信用卡的量，

sentences.text: but that's not true.
sentences.translation: 但那不是真的。

sentences.text: Oh, thank goodness!
sentences.translation: 哦，谢天谢地！

sentences.text: So, my question for you is how long would it really take to ingest that amount of microplastics?
sentences.translation: 那么我的问题是：真正摄入那么多微塑料需要多长时间？

sentences.text: Would it be: a) 13,000 years,
sentences.translation: 选项是：a) 一万三千年，

sentences.text: b) 23,000 years, or c) 33,000 years?
sentences.translation: b) 两万三千年，还是 c) 三万三千年？

sentences.text: Well, I want to be hopeful,
sentences.translation: 嗯，我想乐观一点，

sentences.text: so I'll go with the longest period of time.
sentences.translation: 所以我选最长的那个。

sentences.text: That would be 33,000 years.
sentences.translation: 那就是三万三千年。

sentences.text: OK.
sentences.translation: 好的。

sentences.text: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.translation: 答案会在节目最后揭晓。

sentences.text: So, the World Health Organisation says that microplastics have been found in many different food groups.
sentences.translation: 世界卫生组织说，在许多不同的食物类别中都发现了微塑料。

sentences.text: But Phil, what is the food group that is more affected by microplastics?
sentences.translation: 但是菲尔，受微塑料影响最严重的是哪类食物呢？

sentences.text: Well, scientists have found that seafood is one of the main food groups where microplastics can be found,
sentences.translation: 科学家发现海鲜是微塑料最常出现的主要食物类别之一，

sentences.text: and BBC World Service programme The Evidence has been investigating this.
sentences.translation: BBC世界服务频道的节目《证据》对此进行了调查。

sentences.text: Professor Shilpa Chokshi told host Claudia Hammond about some pictures that she was shown by a microplastics expert.
sentences.translation: 希尔帕·乔克希教授向主持人克劳迪娅·哈蒙德讲了一位微塑料专家给她看的一些图片。

sentences.text: And he showed me all these marine animals that looked like they had plastics in their livers and hind guts.
sentences.translation: 他给我看了这些海洋动物，它们的肝脏和后肠里好像都有塑料。

sentences.text: And from that initial discussion,
sentences.translation: 从那次初步讨论开始，

sentences.text: I went away and I looked at the literature and I looked at the data,
sentences.translation: 我回去查阅了文献和数据，

sentences.text: and there was emerging evidence that there was plastics in the liver,
sentences.translation: 有新出现的证据表明肝脏中存在塑料，

sentences.text: and there was this correlation increase.
sentences.translation: 而且这种相关性在增加。

sentences.text: Shilpa says that plastics have been found in marine animals.
sentences.translation: 希尔帕说，在海洋动物体内发现了塑料。

sentences.text: Marine describes anything related to,
sentences.translation: “海洋的”一词描述任何与海洋相关的、

sentences.text: found in or produced by the sea.
sentences.translation: 在海洋中发现的或由海洋产生的东西。

sentences.text: Yes, these pictures of marine animals with plastics in their bodies inspired Shilpa to dive deeper into the data.
sentences.translation: 是的，这些体内有塑料的海洋动物图片促使希尔帕深入研究数据。

sentences.text: She found emerging evidence,
sentences.translation: 她发现了新出现的证据，

sentences.text: and the adjective emerging describes something coming into view after being hidden,
sentences.translation: 形容词“新出现的”描述某物在被隐藏后逐渐显现，

sentences.text: allowing it to develop or be better understood.
sentences.translation: 使其得以发展或被更好地理解。

sentences.text: And from this emerging evidence,
sentences.translation: 从这些新证据中，

sentences.text: Shilpa noticed a correlation.
sentences.translation: 希尔帕注意到一种相关性。

sentences.text: You'll hear this word a lot when talking about data.
sentences.translation: 在谈论数据时你会经常听到这个词。

sentences.text: A correlation is a link or connection between two or more things.
sentences.translation: 相关性是两个或多个事物之间的联系。

sentences.text: So, Phil, we know how toxic microplastics get into our body,
sentences.translation: 所以，菲尔，我们知道有毒的微塑料是如何进入我们身体的，

sentences.text: but are they definitely harmful?
sentences.translation: 但它们真的有害吗？

sentences.text: Well, plastics have been a big part of daily life since the 1950s,
sentences.translation: 自20世纪50年代以来，塑料一直是日常生活的重要部分，

sentences.text: but it's only recently that we've started thinking about microplastics as a health issue.
sentences.translation: 但直到最近我们才开始把微塑料当作健康问题来看待。

sentences.text: For example, scientists have been looking at people who worked in nylon factories where they were exposed to high levels of microplastic.
sentences.translation: 比如，科学家一直在研究尼龙工厂的工人，他们接触了大量微塑料。

sentences.text: And the scientists think that there may be a correlation between this and diseases that they developed later on.
sentences.translation: 科学家认为这可能与他们后来患上的疾病存在相关性。

sentences.text: Science professor Mark Miodownik,
sentences.translation: 伦敦大学学院的科学教授

sentences.text: from University College London,
sentences.translation: 马克·米奥多尼科夫

sentences.text: has mixed feelings about microplastics and explained these to BBC World Service programme The Evidence.
sentences.translation: 对微塑料看法复杂，他向BBC世界服务频道的《证据》节目解释了这一点。

sentences.text: Well, you know, we have been exposed for decades and surely if it was that bad,
sentences.translation: 你知道，我们已经暴露了几十年，如果真的那么糟，

sentences.text: you know, we'd have seen a spike or something by now.
sentences.translation: 到现在我们应该已经看到问题激增或什么迹象了。

sentences.text: But on the other hand,
sentences.translation: 但另一方面，

sentences.text: you know, I think,
sentences.translation: 你知道，我觉得，

sentences.text: you know, if you look at how much plastic packaging is in supermarkets,
sentences.translation: 如果你看看超市里有多少塑料包装，

sentences.text: it's gone up and up and up and up.
sentences.translation: 它一直在不断上涨、上涨。

sentences.text: And this is not a quantified measure,
sentences.translation: 这虽然不是量化的衡量标准，

sentences.text: but our exposure seems to be increasing,
sentences.translation: 但我们的暴露似乎在增加，

sentences.text: and that's the worry for me.
sentences.translation: 这就是我担心的地方。

sentences.text: Mark mentions that some people say if microplastics were harmful,
sentences.translation: 马克提到，有人说如果微塑料有害，

sentences.text: we surely would have seen a spike in issues related to them by now.
sentences.translation: 到现在我们应该已经看到相关问题激增了。

sentences.text: A spike is literally a pointy shape,
sentences.translation: “激增”字面意思是一个尖尖的形状，

sentences.text: but here it means a sudden,
sentences.translation: 但在这里指突然的、

sentences.text: sharp increase in something.
sentences.translation: 急剧的增加。

sentences.text: Right.
sentences.translation: 对。

sentences.text: And though the amount of plastic packaging we use has increased,
sentences.translation: 尽管我们使用的塑料包装数量增加了，

sentences.text: this isn't a quantified measure.
sentences.translation: 这并不是量化的衡量标准。

sentences.text: If something is quantified,
sentences.translation: 如果某物被量化，

sentences.text: then it's measured and given a number or a value.
sentences.translation: 它就被测量并赋予一个数字或数值。

sentences.text: So, Mark concludes that he is worried about our exposure to plastics.
sentences.translation: 所以马克总结说，他担心我们与塑料的接触。

sentences.text: Exposure means coming into contact with something that may have an impact on you.
sentences.translation: “暴露”指接触可能对你产生影响的东西。

sentences.text: OK.
sentences.translation: 好的。

sentences.text: Phil, so, if people are worried about their exposure to microplastics,
sentences.translation: 菲尔，那么如果人们担心自己暴露于微塑料，

sentences.text: what can they do to reduce this?
sentences.translation: 他们能做些什么来减少接触呢？

sentences.text: Well, one thing they can do is to replace things like plastic chopping boards,
sentences.translation: 他们可以做的一件事是更换塑料砧板、

sentences.text: utensils and food storage containers.
sentences.translation: 餐具和食品储存容器等物品。

sentences.text: And another tip from BBC World Service's The Evidence is to replace tea bags,
sentences.translation: BBC世界服务频道《证据》节目的另一个建议是用散装茶叶代替茶包，

sentences.text: which often contain microplastics, with loose-leaf tea.
sentences.translation: 因为茶包通常含有微塑料。

sentences.text: OK.
sentences.translation: 好的。

sentences.text: Becca, now it's time to get the answer to our quiz question.
sentences.translation: 贝卡，现在是揭晓问答答案的时候了。

sentences.text: And I asked you how long it would take to ingest a credit-card-sized amount of microplastics.
sentences.translation: 我问你摄入一张信用卡大小的微塑料需要多长时间。

sentences.text: Yes, and I said 33,000 years.
sentences.translation: 是的，我说是三万三千年。

sentences.text: OK.
sentences.translation: 好吧。

sentences.text: Well, I've got two bits of bad news for you, Becca.
sentences.translation: 贝卡，我有两个坏消息要告诉你。

sentences.text: One, you were wrong.
sentences.translation: 第一，你答错了。

sentences.text: And two, I'm afraid it's only 23,000 years that it would take to ingest that plastic.
sentences.translation: 第二，恐怕只需要两万三千年就能摄入那么多塑料。

sentences.text: OK.
sentences.translation: 好吧。

sentences.text: Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme,
sentences.translation: 让我们回顾一下本期节目学到的词汇，

sentences.text: starting with marine, which describes anything related to,
sentences.translation: 首先是“海洋的”，描述任何与海洋相关的、

sentences.text: found in or produced by the sea.
sentences.translation: 在海洋中发现的或由海洋产生的东西。

sentences.text: The adjective emerging describes something coming into view after being hidden,
sentences.translation: 形容词“新出现的”描述某物在被隐藏后逐渐显现，

sentences.text: allowing it to develop or be better understood.
sentences.translation: 使其得以发展或被更好地理解。

sentences.text: A correlation is a relationship between two or more things.
sentences.translation: “相关性”是两个或多个事物之间的关系。

sentences.text: A spike is a sudden,
sentences.translation: “激增”指突然的、

sentences.text: sharp increase in something.
sentences.translation: 急剧的增加。

sentences.text: If something is quantified,
sentences.translation: 如果某物被量化，

sentences.text: it's measured and given a number or a value.
sentences.translation: 它就被测量并赋予一个数字或数值。

sentences.text: And exposure means to come into contact with something that may have an impact on you.
sentences.translation: 而“暴露”指接触可能对你产生影响的东西。

sentences.text: Once again, our six minutes are up.
sentences.translation: 我们的六分钟又到了。

sentences.text: Test what you've learned with the worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.translation: 去我们网站bbclearningenglish.com上的练习册测试你学到了什么。

marine.translation: related to, found in or produced by the sea
